key_cases.case_name: Croft v. Westmoreland County Children and Youth Services
key_cases.court: United States Court of Appeals for the Third Circuit
key_cases.holding: The Third Circuit reversed summary judgment for the caseworker, holding that a caseworker who lacked objectively reasonable grounds to believe a child had been abused or was in imminent danger violated the family's Fourteenth Amendment liberty interest by forcing the father to leave the home under threat of removal.
key_cases.relevance: Frames the investigative decision as measured objectively against what the caseworker knew when she acted.
key_cases.quote: Even considered together, minor inconsistencies which provide no affirmative evidence of sexual abuse cannot alone establish the objectively reasonable grounds necessary to remove a family member from the family unit.

key_cases.case_name: Good v. Dauphin County Social Services For Children And Youth
key_cases.court: United States Court of Appeals for the Third Circuit
key_cases.holding: The Third Circuit held that a state child-protective-services immunity statute cannot shield defendants from federal claims, and that a warrantless entry into a home and strip search of a child by a caseworker and police required either freely given consent or exigent circumstances, precluding summary judgment.
key_cases.relevance: Defines the Fourth Amendment limits on how a child-abuse investigation may be conducted.
key_cases.quote: We conclude that: 1) Pennsylvania's Child Protective Services Law cannot immunize defendants from a suit alleging a violation of a federal law

key_cases.court: United States Court of Appeals for the Third Circuit
key_cases.holding: The Third Circuit affirmed judgment for the child-welfare caseworker, holding that a substantive due process claim arising from a child-welfare intervention requires executive conduct that shocks the conscience, a standard that negligence cannot meet.
key_cases.relevance: Establishes that an imperfect or negligent investigation is not by itself a constitutional violation.
key_cases.quote: Critically, under this standard, officials will not be held liable for actions that are merely negligent.

key_cases.case_name: Ernst v. Child and Youth Services of Chester County
key_cases.court: United States Court of Appeals for the Third Circuit
key_cases.holding: Affirming judgment for the agency defendants on the alternative ground of immunity and reversing the judgment entered against the agency's attorney, the Third Circuit held as a matter of first impression that child-welfare workers and counsel representing child-welfare agencies are absolutely immune from section 1983 damages for actions taken in preparing for, initiating and prosecuting dependency proceedings, including formulating and presenting recommendations to the court.
key_cases.relevance: Draws the line between investigative conduct, which carries only qualified immunity, and quasi-prosecutorial case-building, which is absolutely immune from damages.
key_cases.quote: we hold that the CYS defendants are entitled to absolute immunity for their actions on behalf of the state in preparing for, initiating, and prosecuting dependency proceedings

key_cases.case_name: Mulholland v. Government County of Berks
key_cases.court: United States Court of Appeals for the Third Circuit
key_cases.holding: Affirming judgment for the county, the Third Circuit held that the statutory notice, amendment and expungement procedure available to a person listed as an indicated perpetrator on the state child-abuse registry satisfies procedural due process, so the county agency's policy of not forwarding later exculpatory information to the registry was not unconstitutional, and a single caseworker's lapse could not establish municipal liability.
key_cases.relevance: Holds that an allegedly desultory abuse investigation supports no municipal claim absent an agency policy or custom of conducting inadequate investigations.
key_cases.quote: the process provided by the CPSL allows a subject of a report of child abuse the opportunity to air new information at a meaningful time and in a meaningful manner
